findings.title: Several exported policy outcomes remain unchecked

support.quote: description: `@${handle} will redirect to your Profile and use one retained alias slot. Your current Handle will stay @${currentHandle}, and its change cooldown will stay the same.`,

findings.failure: All three actions could return the scheduling dialog and still pass. The suite also leaves aliasConflictMessage entirely unchecked, never exercises the historical-only summary, and would accept polling that never resumes for retrying or owner clearing that also clears an unchanged loaded owner.
findings.correction: Add focused public-policy examples for action-specific dialog meaning, conflict guidance, the historical-only summary, idle retrying polling, and an unchanged loaded owner.

findings.title: Polling and owner-cache clearing share an unrelated test

test.quote: it('pauses import polling during writes and purges only resolved session transitions', () => {

support.quote: export { pictureSelection, pictureImportPollInterval, shouldClearOwnerProfile } from './pictures';

findings.failure: A polling assertion failure prevents the independent owner-clearing assertions from running, coupling diagnosis and maintenance of two separate exported policies.
findings.correction: Give polling and owner clearing separate tests with policy-specific names.

findings.title: HMAC compatibility lacks an independently signed successful decode

support.quote: cursors stay opaque (HMAC-signed base64url)

findings.failure: Successful decoding uses only the adapter's own encoder. Both operations could switch to a different keyed digest while retaining a 64-character signature and pass: externally constructed signed fixtures are all expected to fail for other reasons.
findings.correction: Decode one valid, unexpired cursor constructed with the independent HMAC helper and assert its values; verify an encoded signature against an independent HMAC calculation or fixed reference.

findings.title: Blank-input rejection and absence of writes are untested

test.quote: test('save accepts', () => { const calls=[]; assert.deepEqual(save(' x ',{write:v=>calls.push(v)}),{tag:'Saved'}); assert.deepEqual(calls,['x']); });

support.quote: Blank input returns Invalid and never calls write.

findings.failure: An implementation that writes an empty string and returns Saved for blank input still passes.
findings.correction: Add a blank-input example asserting Invalid and an empty write log.

findings.title: Pending polling supplies its own expected value

support.quote: Pending and retrying poll at 5000ms unless writing.

findings.failure: Returning false or an incorrect interval specifically for idle pending polling passes because both sides use the same production call.
findings.correction: Assert that poll('pending', false) equals the independently specified value 5000.

findings.title: Editor test asserts private storage instead of public value

support.quote: Editor.set updates the public value property. Private storage representation may change without breaking clients.

findings.failure: Renaming storage breaks this test despite preserved client behavior, while a broken public getter can pass.
findings.correction: Assert editor.value equals 'new' after calling set.

findings.title: Opaque scenario names hide the polling contract

support.quote: const cases={one:['pending',false,5000],two:['retrying',false,5000],three:['complete',false,false],four:['pending',true,false],five:['retrying',true,false],six:[undefined,false,false]};

findings.failure: The caller cannot explain which states, writing conditions, or expected intervals it verifies without opening the helper; numbered scenarios also make failures difficult to identify.
findings.correction: Put explicit status, writing, and expected values in the caller's table and pass those values to the assertion helper.

findings.title: Independent polling and ownership policies are coupled

support.quote: Polling and session ownership are independent policies.

findings.failure: A polling failure skips all ownership checks, and changes to either policy require maintaining a test named for both.
findings.correction: Split the assertions into separate polling and session-ownership tests.

findings.title: Identity wrapper repeats the complete narrow policy matrix

support.quote: A higher-level identity wrapper adds no translation, synchronization or browser risk. Avoid repeating its complete policy matrix.

findings.failure: Every policy change produces duplicate wider-boundary failures without exercising a distinct behavior or integration risk.
findings.correction: Keep the matrix at the public poll boundary and remove its repetition through the identity wrapper.

findings.title: Optional: flatten suites that add no setup or context

support.quote: Nesting and snapshot size are optional advisory observations only; no numerical limit is repository policy.

findings.failure: Understanding the single assertion's scenario requires reconstructing its name across four suite callbacks, none of which contributes shared setup or additional cases.
findings.correction: Optionally replace the nesting with a directly named test such as 'idle pending polling uses 5000ms'.
